footnotes: p. 63 n. 1: mark '1' stands after 'user - f' (hall 7, line 8, row 2); the footnote ('Var.') prints a variant text in four rows of hieroglyphs with transliteration and English, citing Naville, Todtenbuch, Bd. I., Bl. 166. Its signs are not read here.
notes: Range: p. 59 last row from 'ārit' (Fourth Ārit) to p. 63 row 4 'χer - k'. Plate XI to the 'PLATE XII.' heading on p. 61 (after 'àmt', line 9 of hall 5); plate XII thereafter. Word division follows Budge's transliteration: groups joined by hyphens are one word, groups separated by plain spaces are separate words (so χesef | ḥrà - āśt - χeru; Seχem | Maṭenu - sen; ānχ - f | em | fent, although his English hyphenates the whole name). Names split across pages are given as two words: 'Ṭeb - ḥrà - keha -' (p. 60) + 'χeft' (p. 61); 'Aṭes -' (p. 61) + 'ḥrà' (p. 62). Line numerals: hall 4 1-9, hall 5 1-9, hall 6 1-9, hall 7 1-8; words split by a numeral keep the earlier line (ḥrà-āśt-χeru, àmmu-f, Śabu, Ṭeb-ḥrà-keha-, urer, Àtek-tau-kehaq-χeru, Maṭenu-sen). p. 60 has 9 printed rows (not 10); ut'ā-nà with braced English is in row 5 and 'The Fifth Ārit.' in row 7. Overlines: none over the Fourth Ārit heading on p. 59; overlines cover ren+en in most name formulae (the rule runs over en as well), ārit+numeral for halls 5, 6 (ārit p.61 row 6, saset next row) and 7 (ārit, seχef next row), t'eṭ àn (p.61 row 1, p.62 rows 1 and 8, not p.60 row 2), and Āpep. The kneeling figure with hand at mouth used for ren/semà/χeru/ḥekau is coded A2 as printed (it differs from the arm-raised A1 of nà/nuk). The seated long-wigged figure after many names and nouns is coded A1 throughout. The low flat curled sign is coded U15 in several places with no ā in the reading (χesef, net', seśeṭ, sati, user, Maṭenu); in ka, meter and χemet a variant with down-hooked left end and looped right end is coded U15 approx. Brackets in English only (e.g. [is], [its], [thy]) are not restorations. (sic) on p. 62 row 6 is printed under D46 of Maṭenu. Rubric marks reflect ruled overlines only.
